items.briefing:
Australia's communications regulator ACMA has taken Optus to Federal Court over a Triple Zero outage in September 2025, highlighting accountability risks for critical service providers. Separately, cybercriminals are increasingly shifting away from ransomware toward simply stealing and selling data — meaning organisations may not get any warning (like a ransom note) that they've been compromised. Finance teams are also being targeted with behavioural attacks that manipulate staff into approving fraudulent transactions.

Researchers warn that many organisations lack proper AI governance frameworks despite growing regulatory pressure — a gap that could create compliance and security risks. **Practical tip:** Remind finance staff never to approve urgent payment requests received by email alone — always verify by phone using a known contact number.

featured.title: ACMA takes Optus to Federal Court over September 2025 Triple Zero outage
featured.quote: ACMA's Federal Court action against Optus sets precedent for Australian telecom accountability.
